description: 100 files in /data show identical modification timestamp. It is a VM snapshot restoration after a hardware incident, documented in an infrastructure ticket, affecting 47 users.
devil_advocate: The attacker caused the 'hardware failure' to force a snapshot restoration, knowing that the identical timestamps would go unnoticed as 'post-restore normalcy'
devil_refutation: The sabotage hypothesis does not explain why the hardware failure was confirmed by the vendor (Dell with warranty claim), why 47 VMs were affected (indiscriminate attack), or why there is no post-restore persistence. The benign explanation is simpler.

peirce_expected.firstness: Multiple files with identical modification timestamp
peirce_expected.secondness: The identical timestamp matches the completion time of a snapshot restoration documented in an infrastructure ticket. 47 VMs are affected, all showing the same pattern. The backup system (Veeam) has logs of the operation.
peirce_expected.thirdness: This is an artifact of mass VM restoration from snapshot. Identical timestamps are characteristic of restore operations, not timestomping. The benign hypothesis explains the scale (100 files, 47 VMs) without requiring malicious coordination.

why_not_malice: The identical timestamps stem from a documented and vendor-verifiable infrastructure event. The scale (47 VMs) is consistent with hardware failure, not a targeted attack.
